contradictions.detail: The listing price field shows $20,500, but the seller's own description says the asking price is $19,500. The correct figure needs confirming.

critical_evidence.evidence: The seller says 'freshly serviced' but shows no dated oil-change or brake-fluid records. A ~9-year-old car with very low annual mileage may never have had its brake fluid changed.
This is a 2017 6MT with an unknown build month. There are no gearbox repair or warranty records and no door-jamb build-date photo.
'Garage-kept' is claimed. There are no photos of lifted footwell carpet, the drain area behind the seats, or the seat-rail bolts (gallery not captured).

Airbag control module software recall 24V695000 (2016-2023 MX-5) applies to this VIN and has no closure proof. Recall 19V072000 covers automatic-transmission TCMs and does not apply to this manual car.
New battery, four zero-mile tires and fresh service are all claimed, with no receipts or DOT/date-code photos.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: the VIN decodes cleanly, the title card reads Clean, and the price is stated, though the two figures conflict. The maintenance half is absent: service, tires and battery are all claimed without receipts or date codes, and there is no history report. The capture is incomplete, so this is not held against the seller.

condition.rationale: No fault is stated, but the only evidence is seller prose ('needs absolutely nothing', garage-kept). Nothing is proven either way on the gearbox, cabin water, leaks or paint.

price_value.rationale: The asking price of $19,500-$20,500 sits below the $22,810-$27,478 fair-value estimate. That estimate leans on ND2 Club/GT Bring a Trailer sales, however. Against the profile's $17-20k California band for a 2017 Sport near 25k miles and the 2016 Sport peers at $20,875-$22,979, it is at market. That makes it fair rather than a bargain, with the early-ND1 gearbox risk unpriced.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, light, reliable roadster priced near the top of the ideal band. It is in California and should resell easily in 6-24 months. The undocumented 2017 6MT history keeps it short of a decisive fit.

logistics.rationale: Napa is a moderate drive from Carmel, the sale is a private CA-registered car, and a local independent PPI should be easy to arrange. The seller has not yet confirmed PPI access or a smog certificate.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Soul Red with a 6-speed is a desirable combination. However, this is base Sport trim without the Club/Brembo/BBS package, and the ND1 engine is the lesser of the two ND engines.

ppi_focus: Warm-gearbox test drive: 2nd/3rd synchro grind, popping out of gear, clutch slip in 4th-6th under load, and engagement height.
Door-jamb build date checked against the early-ND1 gearbox revision period.
Lift footwell carpet and check the seat-rail bolts for corrosion. Clear and water-test both soft-top drains behind the seats.
Soft-top fabric wear at the rear fold corners and header seal; signs of leaks at the seams.
Paint meter on the nose, hood and aluminum fenders for respray. Check stone chips, PPF and wheel curb rash.
Underside check for valve cover, front crank seal and rear diff pinion/output seal seepage, plus water pump weep.
Brake fluid moisture test, and DOT date codes on all four tires and the battery.
Scan for stored codes. Check recall status by VIN, and check Mazda Connect for ghost touch or screen delamination.
Suspension check for end-link and bushing clunks, Bilstein/damper leaks, and an alignment readout.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: dated receipts for the fresh service including brake fluid, tire and battery receipts with date codes, and a closed airbag recall.
Up: a door-jamb build date in mid/late 2017 or documented warranty gearbox work, plus a clean warm-shift PPI.
Up: the price confirmed at $19,500 with a clean history report showing no accidents.
Down: grinding or synchro issues when warm, water in the cabin or corroded seat rails, evidence of respray or accident, or refusal of a PPI.
evidence.mission_note: A manual ND Miata near the top of the ideal price band is a natural enthusiast bridge that should be reliable and quick to resell from Carmel. Its fit depends on the 2017 gearbox history and on proof of time-based maintenance.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2017 MX-5 Sport soft top with a 6-speed manual. The VIN decodes cleanly to match, the car shows 24,800 claimed miles, is in Soul Red, and carries a clean-title card from a private seller in Napa. The only observed inconsistency is the asking price, stated as $20,500 in the price field and $19,500 in the seller text. The maintenance picture rests entirely on seller prose: new battery, zero-mile tires, fresh service and 'needs absolutely nothing', with no receipts, date codes or history report captured. Airbag control module recall 24V695000 applies to this VIN and its closure is unproven; the automatic-transmission recall does not apply. The model's main risk, early-ND1 6MT failures, cannot be assessed until the build month is known and any transmission records are produced. Pricing is roughly at market against the profile band and Sport peers, below an open-class fair-value estimate that is inflated by ND2 Club/GT sales. Cabin water, soft-top wear, paint and leaks remain open because the photo gallery was not captured.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller to confirm the asking price and request photos of the door-jamb build sticker, the service invoice, tire DOT codes and the battery date code, plus recall 24V695000 closure. Then schedule an independent PPI near Napa.
